root_cause.text: The Monaco device tree failed to reserve the full 512 KiB Gunyah hypervisor metadata region at 0x91a80000, leaving part of hypervisor-owned memory marked as normal RAM so Linux could allocate/map PFNs from it and later trigger external aborts when accessed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `gunyah_md_mem: gunyah-md-region@91a80000` with `reg = <0x0 0x91a80000 0x0 0x80000>;` and `no-map;`, while the CVE text says EFI only reserved `0x91a40000–0x91a87fff` but the hypervisor-owned range is `0x91a80000/0x80000`, so the remaining `0x91a88000–0x91afffff` was incorrectly treated as conventional memory and could be allocated by the kernel.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reserve a dedicated no-map memory region for Gunyah metadata to prevent the kernel from using it as normal RAM.
intent_record.what: A new device-tree reserved-memory node named `gunyah_md_mem` was added under `smem_mem`, defining `gunyah-md-region@91a80000` with `reg = <0x0 0x91a80000 0x0 0x80000>;` and marking it `no-map`.
intent_record.how: This reserves a 512 KiB physical memory region starting at 0x91a80000 so the kernel will not map or use it for सामान्य RAM, making it available for the intended Gunyah metadata/firmware use without being touched by the normal memory manager.

grouping_result.intent: Reserve a dedicated no-map memory region for Gunyah metadata to prevent the kernel from using it as normal RAM.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it reserves the Gunyah metadata region as no-map memory so Linux cannot treat hypervisor-owned memory as normal RAM, preventing allocation/mapping of those PFNs and the resulting aborts.

candidates.rationale: This reserved-memory entry only covers 0xF00000 bytes at 0x93b00000 and does not reserve the full Gunyah metadata area at 0x91a80000, leaving hypervisor-owned pages unreserved and potentially usable as normal RAM.

vuln_statements.explanation: This reserved-memory range is too narrow and is placed at 0x93b00000 instead of reserving the full 512 KiB Gunyah metadata region at 0x91a80000. As a result, part of hypervisor-owned memory remained available as normal RAM, allowing Linux to map/allocate PFNs from it and later hit external aborts.

The vulnerable construct is present: under `reserved-memory`, the hypervisor-owned region is not reserved at `0x91a80000` with a full 512 KiB span. Instead, the closest related reservation shown is `smem_mem: smem@90900000 { reg = <0x0 0x90900000 0x0 0x200000>; no-map; }` and then later unrelated reservations like `lpass_machine_learning_mem`, `adsp_mem`, etc. There is no `reserved-memory` entry covering `0x91a80000` for `0x80000` bytes, so the device tree leaves that region unreserved and therefore available as normal RAM. The fix is also absent because there is no explicit reservation or `no-map` entry for the Monaco/Gunyah metadata region at `0x91a80000` in this commit.
